title: Should you pay for multiple AI tools? | Traq Collective
h1: Should you pay for multiple AI tools?
metaDescription: Paying for more than one AI tool is not automatically waste. Check for overlap in who uses it and what job it does before you cancel or add another.
targetQuery: should we pay for multiple AI tools
author: Nazir Dogan
dek: The question is not how many subscriptions you have. It's whether any two of them do the same job for the same person.
intro: Paying for multiple AI tools makes sense when each one does a job the others cannot, like a general assistant for drafting, a coding assistant for a codebase, and an automation platform for workflows. It stops making sense when two tools do the same job for the same person, which is the actual waste worth cutting.

body.heading: What 'too many AI tools' usually means
paragraphs: Most owners who ask this are really asking about cost creep: five or six line items on the card statement, each labeled some AI tool, added one at a time and never reviewed as a set. The fix isn't picking a winner and cancelling the rest. It's checking whether each one earns its seat on its own, not measuring the stack against some arbitrary cap on how many tools a small team is allowed to run.

body.heading: Check what's already bundled before you add a dedicated seat
paragraphs: Before buying a standalone AI subscription, check what your existing software already includes. Microsoft now gives a free, web-grounded Copilot Chat with an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription, and sells a separate paid Copilot add-on for the version that works inside Word, Excel and Outlook on your own data. Google has gone the other way: it folded Gemini directly into its paid Business Standard and Business Plus plans rather than selling it as an extra. If a tool you're about to buy is already half-included in something you pay for, that's the first place to look, not the fourth.

body.heading: When two tools are not actually duplicate spend
paragraphs: A general chat assistant for drafting and research, a coding assistant wired into your actual codebase, and an automation platform that moves data between your other systems are three different jobs. None of them compete for the same task, so running all three at once is not double-paying, it's buying three different capabilities. The confusion starts when people treat 'AI tool' as one category instead of several that happen to share a label.

body.heading: The one test that tells you what to cut
paragraphs: For every AI line item on the bill, write down the one job it does that nothing else you pay for already does. If you can name it, keep the subscription and make sure the right people actually use it. If you can't name it, you've found your duplicate: two tools competing for the same task, usually because one team bought one and another team bought the other without comparing notes first.

takeaway: This week, list every AI subscription on the company card, write next to each one the single job it does that nothing else you pay for already covers, and cancel the ones you can't answer for.

faqs.q: Is it wasteful to pay for both ChatGPT and Claude?
faqs.a: Not automatically. It's wasteful if the same person uses both for the same drafting or research tasks. It's not wasteful if one person standardizes on one assistant while a developer uses the other because it's wired into your coding tools. Check who uses each one and for what before cancelling either.

faqs.q: Should a small business standardize on one AI tool for everyone?
faqs.a: Standardize on one general assistant for the writing and research tasks most people do, since running two of those for the same team rarely adds anything. Specialized tools for coding, automation or meeting notes sit outside that rule because they do a genuinely different job.

faqs.q: Does Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace already include AI?
faqs.a: Yes, to a point. Microsoft includes a free, web-grounded Copilot Chat with eligible Microsoft 365 plans but charges separately for Copilot inside Word, Excel and Outlook. Google now bundles Gemini into its paid Business Standard and Business Plus plans. Check your current plan before buying a standalone AI seat.
